title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Work of Judicial Interpretation
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Judicial Interpretation Work

Fa Fa [2007] No. 12

To all units of this Court:

The Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Judicial Interpretation Work were adopted at the 1408th meeting of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 11, 2006, and are hereby issued to you for implementation.

March 9, 2007

Supreme People's Court

Provisions on Judicial Interpretation Work

I. General Provisions

Article 1 These Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, the Supervision Law of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of the People's Republic of China, the Resolution of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Strengthening the Work of Legal Interpretation, and other relevant provisions, for the purpose of further standardizing and improving judicial interpretation work.

Article 2 Issues concerning the specific application of laws in the trial work of people's courts shall be subject to judicial interpretations by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 3 Judicial interpretations shall be formulated in accordance with laws and relevant legislative intent, taking into account the actual needs of trial work.

Article 4 Judicial interpretations issued by the Supreme People's Court shall be discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee.

Article 5 Judicial interpretations issued by the Supreme People's Court shall have legal effect.

Article 6 The forms of judicial interpretations are divided into four types: "Interpretation", "Provisions", "Reply", and "Decision".

For judicial interpretations formulated on how to specifically apply a particular law in trial work, or on how to apply the law to a certain category of cases or certain issues, the form of "Interpretation" shall be adopted.

For judicial interpretations formulated as norms, opinions, etc., needed in trial work based on legislative intent, the form of "Provisions" shall be adopted.

For judicial interpretations formulated in response to requests from high people's courts and the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army regarding specific issues of law application in trial work, the form of "Reply" shall be adopted.

For amendments or abrogations of judicial interpretations, the form of "Decision" shall be adopted.

Article 7 Where the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate jointly formulate judicial interpretations, it shall be handled in accordance with legal provisions and the opinions agreed upon by both parties through consultation.

Article 8 The Research Office of the Supreme People's Court shall be uniformly responsible for the project initiation, review, coordination, and other work of judicial interpretations.

II. Project Initiation

Article 9 The formulation of a judicial interpretation shall be subject to project initiation.

Article 10 Sources of project initiation for the Supreme People's Court to formulate judicial interpretations:

(1) Requirements put forward by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court for formulating judicial interpretations;

(2) Proposals put forward by the various trial divisions of the Supreme People's Court for formulating judicial interpretations;

(3) Proposals put forward by high people's courts and the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army for formulating judicial interpretations, or requests regarding issues of law application;

(4) Bills or proposals put forward by deputies to the National People's Congress or members of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference for formulating judicial interpretations;

(5) Proposals put forward by relevant state organs, social organizations, other organizations, or citizens for formulating judicial interpretations;

(6) Other circumstances under which the Supreme People's Court deems it necessary to formulate a judicial interpretation.

If a basic people's court or an intermediate people's court considers it necessary to formulate a judicial interpretation, it shall report the matter level by level to the high people's court, which shall review and decide whether to submit a proposal to the Supreme People's Court for formulating a judicial interpretation or to make a request regarding issues of law application.

Article 11 Where the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court requires the formulation of a judicial interpretation, the Research Office shall directly initiate the project.

For other sources of project initiation for formulating judicial interpretations, the Research Office shall review whether to initiate the project.

Article 12 Where the various trial divisions of the Supreme People's Court intend to formulate judicial interpretations of the "Interpretation" or "Provisions" type, they shall submit project initiation proposals for the following year to the Research Office by the end of each calendar year.

The Research Office shall compile the project initiation proposals, draft the annual project initiation plan for judicial interpretations, and submit it to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision after approval by the responsible vice president in charge.

Where special circumstances necessitate adding or adjusting the project initiation of judicial interpretations, the relevant department shall submit a proposal. The Research Office shall report it to the responsible vice president in charge for approval and then submit it to the executive vice president or the President for decision.

Article 13 Where the various trial divisions of the Supreme People's Court intend to formulate a Reply in response to requests from high people's courts or the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, they shall promptly submit a project initiation proposal to the Research Office for review and project initiation.

Article 14 A project initiation plan for judicial interpretations shall include the following: source of initiation, necessity of initiation, main matters requiring interpretation, drafting plan for the judicial interpretation, undertaking department, and other necessary matters.

Article 15 Judicial interpretations shall be completed in accordance with the project initiation plan discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee. If the completion fails to follow the project initiation plan, the drafting department shall promptly submit a written explanation. The Research Office shall report it to the responsible vice president in charge for approval and then submit it to the Judicial Committee to decide whether to continue the project.

III. Drafting and Submission

Article 16 The drafting of judicial interpretations shall be undertaken by the various trial divisions of the Supreme People's Court.

For comprehensive judicial interpretations involving the functional scope of different trial divisions, the Research Office of the Supreme People's Court shall be responsible for drafting, or for organizing and coordinating the relevant departments to draft.

Article 17 In drafting a judicial interpretation, thorough investigation and research shall be conducted, practical experience in trial work shall be conscientiously summarized, and opinions shall be widely solicited.

For judicial interpretations involving the vital interests of the people or major and difficult issues, upon approval by the responsible vice president in charge and reporting to the executive vice president or the President for decision, public solicitation of opinions may be conducted.

Article 18 A draft of a judicial interpretation for review shall be submitted to the relevant special committee of the National People's Congress or the relevant working department of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for solicitation of opinions.

Article 19 Before a draft of a judicial interpretation for review is submitted to the Judicial Committee for discussion, the drafting department shall submit the draft and its explanation to the Research Office for review.

The draft of the judicial interpretation for review and its explanation shall include: the project initiation plan, investigation and research report, status of opinion solicitation, review opinion of the vice president in charge on whether to submit for review, main disputed issues, and relevant laws, regulations, judicial interpretations, and other related materials.

Article 20 The Research Office shall mainly review the following:

(1) Whether it conforms to the provisions of the Constitution and laws;

(2) Whether it exceeds the authority for judicial interpretation;

(3) Whether it duplicates or conflicts with relevant judicial interpretations;

(4) Whether it was carried out in accordance with the prescribed procedures;

(5) Whether the submitted materials meet the requirements;

(6) Whether it fully and objectively reflects the main opinions of the relevant parties;

(7) Whether the main disputed issues and solutions are clear;

(8) Other content that should be reviewed.

The Research Office shall provide a review opinion within one month.

Article 21 If the Research Office considers that a draft of a judicial interpretation for review requires further revision, demonstration, or coordination, it shall conduct revisions, demonstrations, or coordination jointly with the drafting department.

Article 22 After the Research Office reviews the draft of a judicial interpretation for review and forms a draft document, the drafting department shall report it to the responsible vice president in charge and the executive vice president for approval, and then submit it to the Judicial Committee for discussion.

IV. Discussion

Article 23 The Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court shall discuss the draft of a judicial interpretation within three months from the day following its submission. If discussion is overdue, the office of the Judicial Committee may report it to the executive vice president for an extension.

Article 24 Where a draft of a judicial interpretation is discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee, it shall be signed and issued by the President or the executive vice president.

Where a draft of a judicial interpretation is discussed and adopted in principle by the Judicial Committee, the drafting department shall, jointly with the Research Office, make revisions in accordance with the decision of the Judicial Committee. After review by the vice president in charge, it shall be signed and issued by the President or the executive vice president.

If the Judicial Committee considers that the conditions for formulating the judicial interpretation are not yet mature, it may decide on further demonstration, suspend discussion, or cancel the project initiation.

V. Issuance, Implementation, and Filing

Article 25 Judicial interpretations shall be issued in the form of an announcement of the Supreme People's Court.

Judicial interpretations shall be published in the Gazette of the Supreme People's Court and the People's Court Daily.

Judicial interpretations shall come into effect on the date of the announcement, unless otherwise provided in the judicial interpretation.

Article 26 Judicial interpretations shall be filed with the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress within thirty days from the date of issuance.

The General Office shall be responsible for the filing submission work, and the Research Office shall be responsible for other related work.

Article 27 After a judicial interpretation comes into effect, if a people's court uses it as a basis for adjudication, it shall cite it in the judicial documents.

Where a people's court simultaneously cites a law and a judicial interpretation as the basis for adjudication, it shall cite the law first, followed by the judicial interpretation.

Article 28 The Supreme People's Court shall supervise the application of judicial interpretations by local people's courts at various levels and special people's courts in their trial work. A higher people's court shall supervise the application of judicial interpretations by lower people's courts in their trial work.

VI. Codification, Revision, and Abrogation

Article 29 The codification of judicial interpretations shall be decided by the Judicial Committee. The specific work shall be undertaken by the Research Office, with the participation of the various trial divisions.

Article 30 Where a judicial interpretation needs to be revised or abrogated, the matter shall be handled with reference to the relevant provisions of the procedures for formulating judicial interpretations and shall be discussed and decided by the Judicial Committee.

Article 31 These Provisions shall come into effect on April 1, 2007. The Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Judicial Interpretation Work issued on July 1, 1997 shall be simultaneously abrogated.
